2 The objective of the Quantum Computing Certificate program is to prepare those with a degree in a STEM discipline to pivot to a job/career in quantum computing. The demand for a quantum workforce has been emphasized in the National Quantum Initiative Act (https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house- bill/6227). For many of those who might be interested, the option of pursuing an MS or PHD is not possible because of time or expense. This certificate will present the information base to allow a person working in industry or government to advance their careers in an exciting new direction. The four courses are designed to a) refresh a background in math, with an emphasis on the language of quantum mechanics, b) establish a foundation in quantum mechanics, c) apply the foundation to the design of quantum algorithms, and d) expand the knowledge of quantum computing to the technology involved in computation, teleportation, cryptography and circuitry. With this background, a person working with a degree in a STEM discipline will have the opportunity to expand their horizons and become productive in a new field. Our immediate outreach was to NUWC, and they circulated the program to the 8 other warfare centers. The response has been positive. RATIONALE: There should be a demonstrable need for the program.
B1.
Explain and quantify the needs addressed by this program, and present evidence that the program fulfills these needs.
While there are abundant interests and investments in Quantum Computing from the major technology companies (e.g.
Microsoft, Google, IBM…), there are few options for those who want to advance their knowledge.
URI is one of only a handful of universities in the country offering an MS in Quantum Computing.
Yet, for many, the time and expense to pursue a graduate degree is an insurmountable hurdle.
NSF recently had an RFP to encourage universities to begin graduate programs in order to increase the number of trained researchers and to close the perceived gap in personnel with other countries.
Quantum Computing has the potential to revolutionize the way computation is carried out and the economic benefits will be substantial.
Our proposed certificate program gives an additional option.
A student completing the certificate program will have both a foundational understanding as well as the practical knowledge to apply and design quantum algorithms.

In addition, with the embedded project that is threaded through the courses, the student will have a fundamental understanding of more general aspects of quantum sensing, teleportation, cryptography, circuitry and communication B2.
What is the economic need and workforce data related to the program?
The quantum revolution that is taking place will change the way computing is done.
Computations that would require hundreds or thousands of years will be accomplished in minutes on a quantum computer.
For example, the current cryptography protocols, rely on the impossibility of factoring large numbers in any reasonable time.
Quantum computers will be able to do the calculations in near real-time.
The quantum industry needs a workforce to address quantum sensors, quantum networking and communication, quantum hardware, quantum algorithms and the facilitation of technology.
There are 5 main types of technical careers in the quantum industry: engineer, technician, application researcher, experimental scientist, and theorist.
The certificate will support the first three of these job categories.

The number of such jobs posted is well over 100.

July 2020 URI Online – Seed Funding Grant Proposal Program Title: Quantum Computing Department(s)/Sponsoring College(s): Physics/A&S Program Type: UG Degree Completion: # of credits: # of courses: Graduate Certificate: # of credits:12 # of courses:4 Graduate Degree: # of credits: # of courses: Intended Program Start Date: Fall’22 Contact Person: Leonard Kahn E-mail:lenkahn@uri.edu Phone:874-2053 Summary Description of Program (from URI program proposal form): This certificate program is designed for those who have a background in the STEM disciplines to develop an understanding of the the required mathematics, coding, and physics in order to interpret and develop algorithms for Quantum Computing.
The first two courses will help the students pivot to thinking in terms of quantum mechanics, where we anticipate that they have limited experience.
We build on the foundation with the next two courses, where the fundamental approaches to designing algorithms and the hurdles involved in quantum computer design will be presented.
Researchers are currently at the threshold of being able to overcome the inherent fragility of quantum computation.

At the same time advances in quantum circuitry and algorithms are being proposed that will have a significant impact on all of our lives.
Demand for a skilled workforce is a high priority from both government and industrial perspectives, because of national security the anticipated demand for services.
Major bi-partisan legislation supports increasing educational efforts to develop a quantum workforce to maintain the United States’ competitive edge.
This online certificate program complements our traditional face-to-face MS degree program, which is designed for those who will be pursuing a more rigorous training.
The proposed certificate program is targeted for those who are pursuing a career in scientific and/or engineering projects and want to broaden their background in order to take advantage of and contribute to the Quantum Computing revolution.
The four courses in the program are:

July 2020 PHY 571 (online) Math Methods for Quantum Computing: The primary goal of the course is to serve as an introduction to the mathematics that underpins quantum mechanics.
This course will serve as a refresher in linear algebra and introduce the Python computing language.
PHY 572 (online) Quantum Foundations: The primary goal of the course is to serve as an introduction to the foundations of quantum mechanics.
The distinctions between classical and quantum worlds will be described.
The quantum mechanics formalism as it applies to open systems, and its application to quantum computing will be introduced.
Special attention will be paid to entanglement and superposition.
A presentation of how qubits can be represented as vectors terminating on the surface of the Bloch sphere, how they are transformed, and the relation to unitary transformations will be made.
PHY 573 (online) Introduction to Quantum Computing: This course will introduce students to the fundamentals of quantum computing and how it differs from classical computing, including how data is stored, processed and measured.
Basic quantum algorithms will be introduced, and the question of error correction will be discussed.

PHY574 (online) Advanced Quantum Computing: This course presents applications of quantum theory to quantum computing and technology including software and hardware.
More advanced algorithms will be studied within the NISQ (noisy intermediate scale quantum) environment.
Advances in hardware design will be covered.
There will be a common theme through the courses: Students will be developing ever more complex programs using IBM’s online Qiskit, an open-source software development kit, culminating in a project in the 4th semester.
